why: On hard328 the 42-problem gap is mostly the late, ProRL-type part that grows in proportion to a, so a=0.25 recovers only about a quarter of it: 164 + ~10.
With the early part near zero on hard328 and the late part linear in a, a=0.5 recovers about half the 42-problem gap: 164 + ~21.
The orthogonal Code delta supplies the generic early sharpening but none of the math-specific late part, so it adds only a few problems over the cued base's 164 on hard328.
theta(0.5) holds only half of the late part that dominates hard328, so it sits about 21 problems (≈6.5 pts) below RL's 206.
Code-RL lacks the late math part, so on hard328 it stays near the cued base, about 35 problems (≈10.7 pts) below RL plain's 206.
theta(0.5) carries half the late math part and Code-RL carries none, so Code-RL trails theta(0.5) by about 13 problems on hard328.

The shorter-trained 3.0 Math delta already has the saturating early sharpening part, which dominates MATH-500, so with the cue it lands near the a≥0.25 plateau (441-457) even though it has less of the late part.
Any RL run sharpens the base's own distribution early and saturates it, so the Mix delta with the cue lands near the MATH-500 plateau, as Code-RL 3.1 did (450).
Generic sharpening from any RL run turns sometimes-solved MATH-500 problems into reliable ones, so the General delta with the cue should sit near the plateau, well above the cued base's 410.
The orthogonal Code delta supplies the same early sharpening that dominates MATH-500, so the 3.0 Code model with the cue should approach the plateau, as Code-RL 3.1 (450) did.
Under the mechanism any RL run sharpens reliability on base-solvable problems, so the IF delta with the cue should land above the cued base and short of the full plateau.
